title: The Dream of a Eunuch
paragraphs: In the prebifurcated North Arcot District, all the bisexuals from various parts of the country converged for the annual Kūvākam festival commemorating the sacrifice of Aravāṉ. In the festival marked by gaiety, eunuchs, dressed in colourful makeups and dresses, performed the traditional kummi dance in various groups, much to the amusement of gasping youngsters and oldies alike.

The mythology goes that Aravāṉ was sacrificed at the commencement of the Mahābāratha war, and the bisexuals mourned his death with the beating of breasts and the rituals of removing their sacred thread and the sindhur mark on the forehead.

The festival characterized by joyous revelry came to an end as if the end of a storm and the bisexuals all exhausted retired to their restrooms to sleep. A bisexual named Rātā, who was in deep sleep marked by high decibel snoring, had a dream. The eunuch bore the name ‘Rātā’ - common to both male and female persons.

The scene in the dream figured Lord Kaṇṇaṉ and the five Pāṇṭavas with their consort Pāñcāli. As per the condition, the Pāṇṭavas had to live incognito in which they had to be in disguise so that nobody could identify them. Otherwise, they would not regain the countries lost to Turiyōtaṉa by Tarumaṉ in gambling. Therefore, each of the Pāṇṭavas was studiedly sporting the guise by which to hide from public gaze. Among them, Arjuṉaṉ, who was under the cloak of a bisexual, met Lord Kaṇṇaṉ, separately. Yes, all this happened in eunuch Rātā’s dream!
“Kaṇṇa! I have a doubt!”
“What is it Arjuṉā? Do come out with it!”
“Am I a male or a female now?”
“Why do you have such a grammatical confusion, all of a sudden?”
“Would I be called he or she?”
“Hold on! Let me refer to Tolkāppiyam!”
Thus saying Kaṇṇaṉ stretched his hands towards the opposite direction and from nowhere Tolkāppiyam’s palm leaf manuscript came into his hands.
Arjuṉaṉ, who was in the guise of a eunuch posed a question to Kaṇṇaṉ:
“What is this Kaṇṇa? How come Tolkāppiyam exists in this age?”
“O the holder of the bow! In the make-believe world of dreams, everything is possible.”
So saying, Kaṇṇaṉ referred to Tolkāppiyam.
“Look! Tolkāppiyam has an answer to your question!”
“What is the answer? Am I a male or a female?”
“None of the two. Eunuch is the answer.”
“But then, I am a man.”

“Arjuṉā, Tolkāppiyam prescribes that a eunuch deprived of manliness should not be represented by the musculine gender. That is, in expressions like ‘eunuch came, went, spoke, etc., only feminine gender should be used, using the proform ‘she’.”
“What is the verse on that?”
“Here! Listen to me as I read!
> Words denoting > Hermaphroditic ones of effete musculinity > Will not be words with musculine gender endings.”

With disappointment writ large on his face, Arjuṉaṉ beseeched: “Kaṇṇa! Everything is okay. As per Tolkāppiyam, anybody sans manliness should be referred to by feminine gender. But then, in my case, I haven’t lost my manliness to become a bisexual like milk spoilt. I am under the guise of a eunuch only to fulfil the condition imposed by gambling.”
“Therefore, you suppose, you are qualified to be addressed as a man, using the musculine suffix; if that be so, you would be easily identified! Therefore, forbear to
be referred to in feminine terms meant for the eunuch.”
“Great Lord! At least in my case it is an ephemeral phase. But then, how would thousands of eunuchs sans manliness tolerate being referred to in feminine terms?”

“Arjuṉā! Why do you consider feminine gender as degrading? Poor thing, you don’t like women - but Pāñcāli, Alli, Pavaḷakkoṭi, Cupattirai..., the long list of your wives, which certainly doesn’t end with them, all belong to feminine gender!”
An embarrassed and shy Arjuṉaṉ bent his head. Kaṇṇaṉ was quick to retort,
“Well then! Tolkāppiyam’s grammar suits you ninety out of a hundred per cent.”
A startled bisexual Rātā woke up and her mixed dream dissipated.
> Words denoting > Hermaphroditic ones of effete musculinity > Will not be words with musculine gender endings. > > (Collatikāram : Kiḷaviyākkam, verse 12)
